questions.text:
Write an essay on any one of the following in about 150-200 words: (a) Discipline (b) Noise Pollution (c) A Friend in Need is a Friend Indeed (d) Online Education (e) Value of Time
Discipline is the cornerstone of individual character and orderly society. It trains the mind and body to function in adherence to established rules and ethical principles. In academic life, students who cultivate discipline develop regular study habits, achieve excellence, and handle adversity with composure. In professional careers and national defense, it is indispensable for coordination, efficiency, and collective safety. Without discipline, talent goes unharnessed and chaos inevitably ensues; hence, it remains the true foundation of enduring success. OR Noise pollution is an escalating environmental issue caused by urbanization, vehicular traffic, industrial machinery, and uncurbed loudspeakers. Constant exposure to extreme noise levels impairs hearing, elevates stress, and causes hypertension and sleep disturbances. Mitigating this menace requires stringent regulatory enforcement on decibel levels, creation of silent zones around hospitals and schools, and active citizen awareness. OR The proverb "A friend in need is a friend indeed" distinguishes authentic companions from fair-weather acquaintances. A true friend stands steadfast during crises, offering emotional, moral, and practical support without selfish motives. Such loyalty forms the bedrock of genuine human connection and remains a rare, invaluable blessing in life. OR Online education has revolutionized modern pedagogy by transcending geographical constraints through digital technology. It offers unprecedented flexibility, self-paced learning, and access to premier global educators and vast digital repositories. However, challenges like digital divide, screen fatigue, and reduced interpersonal social interaction must be systematically addressed to maximize its efficacy. OR Time is an irrecoverable resource that flows continuously without regard for status or wealth. Utilizing time productively determines whether one achieves greatness or stagnates in regret. Successful individuals recognize the value of each moment through prioritization and punctuality, ensuring that no opportunity is squandered.

questions.text:
Explain any one of the following: (a) "A certain degree of physical harmony and comfort is necessary, but above a certain level it becomes a hindrance instead of help." OR (b) "The voice of my education said to me / He must be killed, / For in Sicily the black, black cobras are innocent, the gold are venomous." OR (c) "There is a house now far away where once / I received love..." OR (d) "The past is not dead and static, it is alive and dynamic..."
(a) This line from Mahatma Gandhi's 'Indian Civilization and Culture' highlights that basic physical comforts are essential for healthy living, but pursuing excessive material luxuries enslaves the human spirit and distracts man from moral and spiritual pursuits. OR (b) In D. H. Lawrence's poem 'Snake', this thought reflects the internal conflict of the poet, whose conditioned human education dictates that a golden Sicilian snake is poisonous and must be killed, even while his instinctive conscience respects the dignified creature. OR (c) Taken from Kamala Das's poem 'My Grandmother's House', these lines express the poet's intense nostalgia for her ancestral home, where she once experienced pure, unconditional love from her late grandmother, in contrast to her present emotional void. OR (d) In 'Bharat is My Home', Dr. Zakir Hussain affirms that our cultural past is neither inert nor obsolete, but remains an active, energetic force that continually guides, shapes, and enriches the quality of our present and future national life.

questions.text:
Explain any one of the following: (a) "In those days, he was not yet a writer; he was merely an employee in a newspaper office." OR (b) "He had the look of being a simple-hearted man as well as a cunning one." OR (c) "The eyes of the people of the world are upon you, and you must not fail." OR (d) "Manners are of more importance than laws."
(a) This passage from Manohar Malgonkar's 'A Pinch of Snuff' depicts the author's early professional days as an Under-Secretary on probation, describing his modest beginnings before gaining literary stature. OR (b) Taken from H. E. Bates's 'The Earth', this sentence describes the dual demeanor of Johnson, Benjy's father, who outwardly seemed simple and innocent, yet harbored subtle craftiness in his rural life. OR (c) In Martin Luther King, Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream', this reflection underscores the historic moral obligation resting on American civil rights activists to nonviolently dismantle systemic racism before the watchful global community. OR (d) This observation highlights that while laws merely penalize external misconduct, cultured personal manners and everyday courtesy determine the moral fabric, dignity, and harmony of civil society.

questions.text:
Write an application to your Principal requesting him to issue your School Leaving Certificate (SLC). OR Write a letter to your friend describing your visit to a historical place.
To: The Principal, [School Name], [City]. Respected Sir, I respectfully submit that I have passed the Intermediate Examination from your esteemed institution this year. As I now need to seek admission into an undergraduate degree program at an external university, I kindly request you to issue my School Leaving Certificate (SLC) at your earliest convenience. All my outstanding dues have been cleared. Thanking you, Yours obediently, [Your Name]. OR Dear [Friend's Name], I am thrilled to share my recent visit to the historic city of Agra. Standing before the majestic Taj Mahal at sunrise was an unforgettable sight; its translucent white marble and intricate floral inlay work were breathtaking. We also explored the formidable red sandstone ramparts of Agra Fort, which brought Mughal history vividly alive. I truly missed your company and hope we can plan our next historical trip together. Warm regards, [Your Name].

(c) How did Nanukaka impress the minister? (d) What did Bertrand Russell say about the survival of the human species? (e) Why does John Donne want to go away? questions.modelAnswer:
wer any five of the following in about 40-50 words each: (a) What did the author mean by saying that 'India was in his blood'? (b) Why did Seibei wander about the town? (c) How did Nanukaka impress the minister? (d) What did Bertrand Russell say about the survival of the human species? (e) Why does John Donne want to go away? (f) How does the poet describe the cat Macavity? (g) What happens in autumn according to Keats? (h) What is the poet's regret in 'Snake'? (i) Name two major Middle English dialects. (j) Write a short note on Old English.
(a) In 'India Through a Traveller's Eyes', Pearl S. Buck states that India was in her blood because she grew up listening to intimate family accounts of Indian life, traditions, and culture from her doctor parents.
(b) In Shiga Naoya's story 'The Artist', Seibei was passionately obsessed with gourds and tirelessly wandered around town searching for symmetrical, uniquely shaped gourds displayed in curio shops and fruit-seller stalls.
(c) Nanukaka impressed the minister by arriving in a chauffeur-driven luxury car, dressing flamboyantly like an aristocrat, and registering himself in the visitor's book as the hereditary astrologer to the Maharaja of Ninnore.
(d) In 'Ideas That Have Helped Mankind', Bertrand Russell observed that early humans faced grave physical hazards and starvation, but intelligence and language enabled them to survive and dominate other species.
(e) In 'Sweetest Love I Do Not Goe', John Donne departs not out of weariness of his beloved, but to rehearse and prepare for the ultimate, inevitable separation of mortal death through voluntary absence.
(f) T. S. Eliot depicts Macavity as a tall, thin feline master criminal with sunken eyes, a deeply lined brow, uncombed whiskers, and dusty coat, famously nicknamed 'The Hidden Paw'.
(g) In 'Ode to Autumn', Keats describes autumn conspiring with the sun to ripen fruits, swell gourds, fill hazel shells with sweet kernel, and bloom late flowers for the bees.
(h) In 'Snake', D. H. Lawrence regrets throwing a crude log at the harmless, majestic snake out of petty, conditioned human instincts, feeling remorse for violating an honored king of the underworld.
(i) Two major Middle English dialects were the Northern dialect and the East Midland dialect.
(j) Old English (AD 449–1066) was a purely Germanic inflected tongue characterized by complex case endings, a distinct runic script, and limited Celtic/Latin vocabulary, which eventually evolved into modern English.

Whitman perceives his own body and soul as inseparable from the rest of humanity, declaring that every atom belonging to him belongs equally to every human being. He rejects artificial social hierarchies and dogma, seeking spiritual communion with open cosmic nature. OR 'Ode to Autumn' by John Keats portrays autumn as a season of mists, ripeness, and serene maturity working in harmony with the sun. OR 'The Soldier' by Rupert Brooke is a patriotic war sonnet in which an English soldier reflects on death abroad. questions.modelAnswer:
wer the questions that follow: Education is not just about gaining knowledge, but about developing critical thinking and building strong moral character. It equips individuals with the skills necessary to navigate life's challenges, empowering them to make informed decisions and contribute positively to their communities. Beyond professional success, a good education fosters empathy, open-mindedness, and civic responsibility. Questions: (a) What is education truly about? (b) How does education empower individuals? (c) What values does education foster besides professional success? (d) Make sentences with: (i) Empathy (ii) Challenge. OR Write a précis of the following passage and give a suitable title: Reading books is one of the finest habits a person can cultivate. It enriches the mind, broadens horizons, and enhances vocabulary. Books introduce readers to new ideas, cultures, and philosophies, stimulating imagination and creativity. Moreover, regular reading improves concentration and reduces stress, offering a healthy mental escape from the pressures of everyday life. In an era dominated by digital distractions, dedicating time to read remains an essential practice for personal growth and intellectual well-being.
(a) Education is truly about developing critical thinking, building strong moral character, and gaining essential knowledge.
(b) It empowers individuals by equipping them with vital skills to navigate life's challenges and make informed decisions.
(c) Besides professional success, it fosters empathy, open-mindedness, and civic responsibility.
(d) (i) Empathy: True leaders listen to others with genuine empathy. (ii) Challenge: She was determined to overcome every challenge in her career.
OR
Title: The Benefits of Reading Books.
Précis: Reading is an invaluable habit that enhances vocabulary, stimulates intellectual creativity, and broadens cultural understanding. It builds concentration, alleviates daily stress, and serves as an indispensable tool for personal growth amidst digital distractions.
